_comment: Recording of live run 41 (status partial); the plan is the model's own words.

steps.message: Reviewing the intake and the question.

claims.text: Whether solar can go on this roof is not yet settled. The roof is pitched (not flat), the city's roof review rates the library 'Not Solar Ready', and the city's records flag the building as a landmark. Solar size, output and cost cannot be estimated until an engineer or roofer verifies the usable roof area and enters it in the intake. The roof cannot be certified from these records. A licensed structural engineer or architect (PE/RA) must do that analysis.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: The goal is a 30% cut in grid electricity by 2030 on a $500,000 capital budget. A standard efficiency package alone is estimated to cut about 6.2% to 17.6% of annual electricity use. That is about 21% to 59% of the way to the goal, so it does not reach the goal by itself.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The efficiency package typically costs $47,092 to $161,804, which fits inside the $500,000 budget. Closing the rest of the gap to 30% would likely need solar, which cannot be sized yet. Whether the budget should be extended is a decision for the library once solar is sized and compared with its savings.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The city's records show a landmark flag for this lot. A Landmarks Preservation Commission review is needed before any rooftop or exterior work. The records do not confirm which historic district the building sits in; the Greenwich Village Historic District is the user's statement.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Entered by the user: Jefferson Market Library (NYPL), 425 6th Avenue, Manhattan; library; 18,643 sq ft; built 1877; pitched roof of 7,020 sq ft; Con Edison customer; annual grid use 268,331 kWh (kWh is energy used over time); capital budget $500,000 for 2027; critical loads are reading room cooling and lighting.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The user listed no existing solar, other renewables or efficiency work. The plan assumes none exist already. Please confirm, along with whether lighting is already LED.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: The baseline for the goal is the electricity the building buys from the grid. The city's Local Law 84 energy report for 2024 shows 268,331 kWh of electricity for this library, which matches the entered figure. It is treated as measured use.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The city's lot record lists the street address as 421 Avenue of the Americas, while the address entered was 425 6th Avenue. This can be another frontage of the same lot. It also shows 19,800 sq ft of gross floor area against 18,643 sq ft entered and reported in the energy report. The entered figure is the working figure; please confirm.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: City building footprints show one building on the lot with a ground footprint of 7,019 sq ft, close to the 7,020 sq ft roof area entered. A footprint is the ground area under the building, not a measured roof, and for a pitched roof the real surface and usable area differ. The roof area is the user's number and must be verified by an engineer or roofer.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The city's solar-readiness record for the owning agency (NYPL) lists this library as 'Not Solar Ready', with roof condition and roof age both 'Unknown'.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Efficiency measures (LED and controls) save 10-20% of annual use. This is a planning estimate, not a cited benchmark and not a building model.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Planning-level benchmark prices, not quotes: solar $3,131-4,668 per kW (kW is how much power at one moment) from the middle half of 558 completed NYC non-residential projects of 25-100 kW since 2022 (NYSERDA data); battery $600-1,000 per kWh (planning estimate); efficiency cost per kWh saved per year $1.17-4.02 (standard) from the middle half of completed NYC public-sector projects since 2016 (NYSERDA data). Standard efficiency saving is 10-20% and deep is 15-25%; these percents are planning estimates, and only 62%-88% of them is counted because the City's audited projects delivered that share (NYC DCAS Local Law 87 report, FY2022).
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Baseline grid use is 268,331 kWh a year, treated as measured because it matches the city's energy report. The 30% goal applies to electricity only.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: A standard efficiency package (LED lighting and controls) is estimated to save about 16,637 to 47,226 kWh a year, which is 6.2% to 17.6% of annual use. The underlying 10-20% saving is a planning estimate. Only 62% to 88% of predicted savings is counted, because the City's own audited projects delivered that share (NYC DCAS Local Law 87 report, FY2022). The trimmed share is not added back.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Lighting type, cooling type, building controls and the year the roof was last replaced were left blank in the intake. If LED lighting is already installed, it should not be counted again, and the savings and their confidence would be lower. Please provide these details.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: The building also burns natural gas: 1,041,151 kBtu (thousand BTU) in the 2024 energy report. Heating fuel is outside an electricity-use goal, so gas use is not counted toward the 30% cut.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The roof is pitched, so the roof-sizing calculation refused to run. No roof area, array size, solar output or solar savings is given here, and nothing was estimated in their place.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Next step: an engineer or roofer verifies the usable roof area (size, pitch, direction, structure, shading) and enters it in the intake. Then the plan is re-run. Once re-run, real solar output will still depend on the roof pitch and direction, so confidence stays lower than for a flat roof.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: The city's solar-readiness record rates the library 'Not Solar Ready' with unknown roof condition and age. The roof should be checked, and replacement considered, before solar. None of the cost totals in this plan include roof repair or replacement; a roofer's quote is needed.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: NYC's sustainable roofs rule (Local Laws 92 and 94 of 2019) applies to existing buildings undergoing certain major roof renovations: the roof must carry a solar system, a green roof, or both. If the roof is replaced, this rule may apply and should be checked with the Department of Buildings.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Scenario A (efficiency only): reduces annual use by about 6.2% to 17.6%, which is 21% to 59% of the 30% goal. It does not reach the goal.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario A cost: the typical range is $47,092 to $161,804; the median of similar NYC projects is about $103,039. No incentive is counted, so net cost is the same. Annual savings are about $3,296 to $11,419 using the New York commercial average price. Simple payback is about 4.1 to 49.1 years, with about 14 years at the median. This is a simple payback, not a full solar-and-efficiency simulation.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario A budget strain: within budget, using about 9% to 32% of the $500,000. The model treats the budget as one total upfront amount. Scenario A gives no backup power (0 outage hours).
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenarios B (efficiency plus solar within budget) and C (deep efficiency, full roof array and battery) were not costed. They depend on solar output, which needs the verified usable roof area. They will be compared once that area is entered. Rooftop solar alone typically covers only about 15-25% of annual use and would not reach a 30% goal by itself; the share for this roof is unknown until then.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: The plan cannot say yet whether the full path to 30% fits $500,000. If it costs more, the gap will be shown against the savings. Meeting the goal may take more than the budget; whether to extend it is the library's decision.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Standard efficiency package: typical range $47,092 to $161,804; the median of similar NYC projects is about $103,039. Basis: about 40,250 kWh saved a year (the middle of the 10-20% planning estimate) times $1.17 to $4.02 per kWh saved, from the middle half of completed NYC public-sector LED-lighting and comprehensive projects since 2016 (NYSERDA data). These are planning-level figures, not quotes.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Solar and battery cost lines are not given because the array cannot be sized for a pitched roof until the usable area is verified. No roof repair or replacement is included in any cost total.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Federal elective pay (direct payment of the solar investment credit to governmental entities) is listed as open as of 2026-10-18, but solar must be placed in service by 2027-12-31. Whether this library or its agency qualifies is not confirmed. It is left out of net cost until solar is sized and eligibility is confirmed. The 2027 deadline is tight for a landmark roof that needs structural, roof and Landmarks reviews.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The NYSERDA NY-Sun commercial solar incentive for the Con Edison region has uncertain status: its dashboard could not be read automatically as of 2026-10-18. It is left out of net cost. Check the dashboard in a browser before counting any incentive.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The budget is a capital budget for 2027. The model treats it as one total upfront figure, not year by year.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Savings use the New York commercial average price of about $0.1981 to $0.2418 per kWh (12-month average about $0.222), not this building's own tariff.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Phase 0, confirm data and budget: confirm the annual bills, the budget year (2027) and type (capital), which Con Edison tariff is on the bill, existing systems, lighting type and the year the roof was last replaced.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 1, professional reviews: a licensed structural PE or RA analysis of the roof, plus a roof condition survey, with the usable solar area verified and entered in the intake. Landmarks Preservation Commission review should begin at this stage.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 2, efficiency measures: install the standard efficiency package (LED lighting and controls, minus anything already done), then track results against bills.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 3, permits and Con Edison interconnection: Department of Buildings permits, a licensed electrician, FDNY rooftop access review, Landmarks approval, and the Con Edison interconnection application.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 4, solar installation: only after the reviews, roof repairs if needed and approvals are done, and after the plan is re-run with the verified roof area.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 5, battery, commissioning and verification: size a battery for the reading room cooling and lighting once the load in kW and backup hours are given, then check results against bills.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Scenario A gives no backup power. Scenario B would not either, because solar panels shut off in an outage without a battery. Scenario C, with a battery, was not run, so no outage hours are available for it.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The critical loads named by the user are reading room cooling and lighting. The critical load in kW and the backup hours wanted were left blank, so no battery is sized yet.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The current FEMA flood map shows zone X (area of minimal flood hazard) at this address. Only the flood zone was read. Heat and winter-storm ratings were not looked up, and the 2015 preliminary flood map was not checked, so the flood result is partial.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: A licensed structural PE or RA must analyze whether the roof can carry panels. This plan cannot certify the roof.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: A roof condition survey is needed, because the city rates the roof's condition and age as unknown and the library 'Not Solar Ready'. Repair or replacement may come before solar.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: A Landmarks Preservation Commission permit review is needed before any rooftop or exterior work, because the city record flags this lot as a landmark. Panels on a pitched, visible historic roof are likely to get close review. If the site is also on parkland, the Commission gives the owning agency an advisory report instead of a permit; confirm this with the owner.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Other required steps: a licensed electrician, FDNY rooftop access review, Department of Buildings permits, and a Con Edison utility interconnection review. The owner agency was not entered; confirm the approval route with NYPL and the city owner. Links to each office are in the contact list at the end of the plan.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: A flood-zone review under the NYC Building Code is not triggered by the current FEMA map (zone X). The preliminary map was not checked, and NYC code uses the more restrictive map.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

sections.title: Path to net-zero and learning resources

claims.text: The library uses much more energy as natural gas (1,041,151 kBtu) than a 30% electricity cut addresses. Long-term net-zero would also need a plan for heating, such as electrifying it, which is not modeled here.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: The next step toward the goal is to verify the roof area, complete the reviews, and re-run the plan with solar and battery scenarios.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: The roof-sizing calculation failed because the roof is pitched and no verified usable roof area was entered. As a result there is no usable roof area, array size, solar output, solar savings, or cost for scenarios B and C. The solar production lookup was not run for the same reason. Next step: enter the verified usable roof area and re-run the plan.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Scenario A contains no solar, so no solar sizing or output figure enters any of its results.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The city's address for this lot (421 Avenue of the Americas) differs from the address entered (425 6th Avenue). It can be another frontage of the same lot. The city's gross floor area of 19,800 sq ft also differs from the 18,643 sq ft entered; the entered figure is kept, please confirm.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The electricity price is the New York commercial average, not this building's tariff. The utility lists several general-service tariffs for NYC, and which applies depends on peak demand, voltage and meter. The tariff must be confirmed on a bill (listing as of 2026-10-18, effective dates 2025-02-01).
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Roof replacement year, roof condition, owner agency, lighting type, cooling type, controls, heating fuel, goal type, critical load in kW, backup hours and the building's own electricity price were left blank. Confidence is lower for claims that depend on them.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The incentive list is a curated register kept by a person, with official pages re-read on 2026-10-18. NY-Sun could not be confirmed and is uncertain; federal elective pay is open but eligibility is unconfirmed. Neither is counted in net cost.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Efficiency savings are planning estimates with low confidence. Only the flood zone was read; heat and winter-storm ratings were not checked. No page with hidden instructions was found. Every figure is an estimate range, and none is a promise of savings.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

roadmap.footer_note: All figures are planning estimates in ranges, not quotes and not promises of savings. Simple payback is not a full solar simulation. The roof cannot be certified here; a licensed PE or RA must review it.
